purpose: Educational comparison of published central concentrations, not a reference interval engine.

pediatric.population: Residual hospital samples; patients investigated for DSD or other endocrinopathy excluded. Not a healthy population birth cohort.
notes: Illustration midpoint is a display convention, not a reported sample age or model knot.
These are small cross-sectional groups. Small reversals between adjacent medians must not be presented as established biological peaks or troughs.
Infant groups were not selected because the 2022 female longitudinal cohort offers better resolved infant serum medians.

adult.source: Beckman Coulter Access AMH, FDA K170524 (2017), Expected Reference Intervals
adult.assay: Beckman Coulter Access AMH on Access 2
adult.population: Apparently healthy nonpregnant females at five sites, regular 21–35-day menstrual cycles, both ovaries present, proven fertility.
notes: Not an all-women population estimate: participants were selected for regular cycles and proven fertility.
Do not silently alternate serum and plasma values. The paper on pediatric Access medians used plasma; the detailed infant cohort used serum.
Source does not provide median concentrations above 45 years. Do not extrapolate numeric concentrations into menopause or old age.
The maximum group median occurs at 26–30 years; these data do not locate an exact peak at age 28.

recommendation: Keep source/matrix provenance and distinguish interpolated display connections from observed/modelled age-specific data. Use plasma for both Jopling and adult Access if a single same-matrix older series is wanted; keep infant serum identified separately. No assay conversion or arbitrary amplitude adjustment.
